learning: Iterations 2 to 4 found that footprint, span, look-ahead to 0.06 m, and wheel_track do not move max_error (about 0.061 m). If max_error falls below about 0.058 m with line loss at zero, yaw inertia is a real limit. If it does not move, the excursion is a start-up transient or fixed bias and the next step is a start-up geometry test. Report whether the excursion occurs at the start of the run or at a specific bend.
notes: Iteration-2 controller and y = 0.04 geometry, with the Builder's single change: mass 0.8 to 0.6 kg, testing whether yaw inertia sets the 0.061 m excursion. wheel_track is reverted to 0.12 m because 0.15 m gave no gain. Controller is unchanged, so any shift in max_error is attributable to mass.
rationale: Iteration 2 is the best-scoring pairing so far (26.9949): 16 mm sensors at x = ±0.05 m, y = 0.04 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, kp 3.5, ki 0, kd 0.05. Iteration 4 showed that wheel_track 0.15 m with kp 4.4 gives the same max_error (0.0614 oval, 0.0611 s-bend, 0.0609 slalom) and higher control effort, so I revert the track to 0.12 m. Iteration 3 showed that y = 0.06 brought back line loss and did not move max_error, so y stays at 0.04 m. The Builder's one change is mass 0.8 to 0.6 kg. That changes the dynamics, not the sensing or the steering gain, so I keep the iteration-2 controller unchanged (kp 3.5, ki 0, kd 0.05, base_speed 1.6, last_direction, weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1]). I do not apply kp scaling for mass, because the Integrator has no evidence that mass changes the effective steering gain. Off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.12/4) = 0.06 m, so body_width stays 0.12 m. Expected result is not stated: this race should show whether max_error responds to yaw inertia, with line loss expected to stay at zero, and I will report whether any excursion sits at the start of the run or at a particular bend.
